newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply higher.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures contracts ended sharply higher on Monday, with the September contract rising by its daily 500 yen limit, traders said.
The benchmark March 1998 contract closed 470 yen higher at 16,340 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 46,313 lots.

All contracts fell during the morning session due to light technical selling from local investors, traders said. But price rises in CBOT overnight trading triggered active buying by late afternoon, they said.
Some traders cited technical buying orders from U.S. investment funds as behind the price gains.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.00-3/4 per bushel at 0855 GMT, against $2.96-3/4 at Friday's close.
The CBOT soybean futures spot March contract was at $8.04 at 0855 GMT, up from $7.91 at Friday's close.
